title: Single-Stage Amplifiers
intro: Complex amplifiers are built from four basic stages: common source, source follower, common gate and cascode. Learn each stage's gain, input and output impedance and headroom.

blocks.text: An amplifier is evaluated by its gain, bandwidth, input and output impedance, noise, linearity and output swing. Single-stage amplifiers are the building blocks, and the properties below are what each stage offers:

items: Common source: voltage gain -gm*(RD||ro), high input and output impedance, the most used stage.
Source follower: gain below one, high input and low output impedance (buffer).
Common gate: low input impedance, non-inverting, current buffer.
Cascode: very high output impedance and gain, limited swing.

blocks.text: Ask what impedance the stage must see on each side. A voltage amplifier with a high-impedance source needs a gate input (CS or follower). A current source driving a load wants a high Rout (cascode). A low-impedance source needs a low Rin (CG).
Quick table: CS gives voltage gain; SF gives impedance transformation; CG gives current buffering; cascode gives output impedance. Everything else is a combination of these.

blocks.title: Pick the stage
blocks.text: You need to drive a 50 ohm load from a high-impedance sensor with a voltage gain of about 1 and little loading of the sensor. Which stage (or stages) fits?
solution: A source follower: its gate presents a high input impedance to the sensor, and its output impedance 1/(gm+gmb) is low. To drive 50 ohm directly you would need gm of about 20 mS, which takes a large current, so in practice a follower is the last stage with a large device and bias current.
